newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway c. bank could see lower money market rates.
newsitem.headline: Norway c. bank could see lower money market rates.

text.p: Norway's central bank, which is under pressure to cut official interest rates, said on Tuesday its currency policy was no reason why Norwegian money-market rates could not fall below the German equivalents.
But this could not happen without a Norwegian interest rate cut, said Leif Eide, chief of market operations at the bank.
He declined, however, to speculate whether key official interest rate would be cut to keep the Norwegian crown from appreciating too much.
"The central bank's policy of currency stability is no reason why German rates should form the floor for Norwegian money-market rates," Eide told Reuters.
The primary objective of Norwegian monetary policy is exchange rate stability.
Eide was elaborating on a statement to Norwegian daily Aftenposten, which quoted him as saying there was no reason why short money-market rates could not fall below the German ones.

Analysts said the statement helped sending Norwegian three-month eurokrone swap rates down 10 basis point to 3.53 percent on Tuesday morning, narrowing the gap to the German three-month rate to about 40 basis points.
"It is possible for Norwegian money-market rates to fall below German rates, but whether that is good for the Norwegian economy is another matter," Eide told Reuters.
"If money-market rates are to be below the German ones, then official interest rates must be reduced," Eide said.
Analysts said the market had discounted for a 50 basis point cut in official interest rates.
The central bank's rate on overnight deposits, now 4.0 percent, normally sets the floor for money market rates.
The bank last cut the deposit and another key rate on November 6 by 0.5 percent respectively to hem in the crown, which is buoyed by the strong Norwegian economy.

But the move did not stop the crown, which stood at 101.17 on the inverse ECU index when the rate cut was announced two months ago. On Tuesday morning the crown, which is in a dirty float, had firmed to about 100.75 on the same index.
The bank worried about cutting rates for fear of fuelling inflation and has instead been selling billions of crowns recently in an attempt to offset the crown's strength.
